Trey Research Vendor Agreement — TR-EA-2026-0417 — CONFIDENTIAL
TREY RESEARCH VENDOR AGREEMENT
Version 4.2 — Document ID: TR-EA-2026-0417
Dated as of October 16, 2026
By and Between
TREY RESEARCH a Delaware corporation 8500 Shoal Creek Boulevard, Building 3 Austin, TX 78757
("Vendor")
and
ZAVA, INC. a Delaware corporation 200 Harborview Drive, Suite 1400 Stamford, CT 06902
("Company" or "Customer")

RECITALS
WHEREAS, Trey Research ("Vendor") is in the business of developing, operating, and licensing machine-learning-as-a-service platforms, including the proprietary decisioning engine known as "Trey Research AI Platform," and Vendor possesses substantial expertise, intellectual property, and technical infrastructure related to the design, deployment, and operation of such platforms;
WHEREAS, Zava, Inc. ("Company") desires to license and deploy the Trey Research AI platform to support its internal business operations, including automated decisioning processes that rely upon machine-learning-based inferential outputs; and
WHEREAS, the parties wish to set forth the terms and conditions under which Vendor will provide the Trey Research AI platform and related implementation, training, support, and maintenance services to Company, and under which Company will access and use such platform and services in accordance with the rights, obligations, and restrictions described herein.
NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:
SECTION 1 — DEFINITIONS
As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Section 1 shall have the meanings ascribed to them elsewhere in this Agreement.
"Agreement" means this Trey Research Vendor Agreement, Version 4.2, Document ID TR-EA-2026-0417, together with all Exhibits attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference, as each may be amended from time to time in accordance with Section 23.2.
"Trey Research AI Platform" or "Platform" means Vendor's proprietary machine-learning-as-a-service decisioning engine, including all software, algorithms, Models, application programming interfaces, user interfaces, tools, dashboards, and documentation made available by Vendor as part of the Services, as further described in Exhibit A (Service Description & SLA).
"Company Data" means all data provided by Company or its authorized users to Vendor in connection with the Services, including without limitation input data, configuration data, metadata, and any data generated as a result of Company's use of the Platform, but excluding Models, Model Derivatives, and any aggregated or anonymized data that is not reasonably identifiable as relating to Company or any individual.
"Confidential Information" has the meaning set forth in Section 10.1.
"Decision" means a single inferential output generated by the Platform in response to a submitted input request, as metered and recorded by Vendor's internal monitoring systems. For the avoidance of doubt, each discrete inferential output constitutes a separate Decision regardless of whether multiple Decisions are submitted in a single batch or API call.
"Deliverables" means all outputs, reports, analyses, configurations, and work product produced by Vendor pursuant to and in connection with a Statement of Work.
"Effective Date" means December 13, 2026.
"Fees" means, collectively, the Implementation Fee, the Annual Platform Fee, any Overage Fees, and any other amounts payable by Company under Section 4 and Exhibit B (Fee Schedule & Order Form).
"Implementation Fee" means the one-time implementation fee set forth in Section 4.1 and Exhibit B.
"Annual Platform Fee" means the recurring annual fee for access to and use of the Platform as set forth in Section 4.2 and Exhibit B, as adjusted annually in accordance with the annual escalator described therein.
"Model(s)" means any machine learning model, algorithm, neural network, statistical model, ensemble model, large language model, or similar technology developed, trained, deployed, or made available by Vendor through the Platform, including without limitation all weights, parameters, hyperparameters, architectures, configurations, and associated training and validation methodologies.
"Model Derivatives" means any derivative, fine-tuned, adapted, retrained, distilled, compressed, or modified version of a Model, whether created using Company Data, third-party data, Vendor's proprietary data, or any combination thereof.
"Outputs" means the inferences, predictions, scores, classifications, recommendations, rankings, and other results generated by the Platform in response to Company's input data, including any formatted reports or visualizations derived therefrom.
"Overage Fee" means the per-Decision fee applicable to Decisions exceeding the Monthly Decision Volume Threshold in any calendar month, as set forth in Section 4.3 and Exhibit B.
"Monthly Decision Volume Threshold" means four million (4,000,000) Decisions per calendar month.
"Services" means, collectively, the provision of access to and use of the Platform, implementation services, integration support, training, technical support, maintenance, and all related services as described in this Agreement and Exhibit A.
"SOC 2 Report" means the Service Organization Control 2 report described in Section 12.2 and Exhibit C (Security Standards & SOC 2 Reporting).
"Statement of Work" or "SOW" means any statement of work, work order, or project plan executed by the parties pursuant to this Agreement that describes specific implementation or professional services to be performed by Vendor.
"Subcontractor" means any third party, including any affiliate of Vendor, engaged by Vendor to perform any portion of the Services or to process Company Data on Vendor's behalf.
"Term" has the meaning set forth in Section 15.
Additional defined terms used throughout this Agreement with initial capitalization shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the context in which they appear.
SECTION 2 — SCOPE OF SERVICES
2.1 Platform Access. Vendor shall provide Company with access to and use of the Trey Research AI platform for the purpose of automated decisioning, subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement. The features, functionality, and technical specifications of the Platform are further described in Exhibit A (Service Description & SLA). Company's access to and use of the Platform shall be limited to Company's internal business operations and shall be subject to the restrictions set forth in Section 3.4 and Exhibit D (Acceptable Use Policy).
2.2 Services Included. The Services provided under this Agreement include the following: (a) access to and use of the Platform, including all core modules, APIs, and supported integrations as described in Exhibit A; (b) implementation services, including environment provisioning, data ingestion pipeline configuration, model configuration, integration testing, and user training as described in the applicable Statement of Work; (c) ongoing technical support in accordance with the support terms set forth in Exhibit A; and (d) such other services as may be mutually agreed upon by the parties in writing from time to time.
2.3 Service Levels. Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to make the Platform available in accordance with the service levels set forth in Section 5 and Exhibit A. Vendor's service level obligations are subject to the limitations, exclusions, and remedies set forth in Sections 5 and 6 of this Agreement and the corresponding provisions of Exhibit A.
2.4 Implementation. Vendor shall perform the implementation services described in the applicable Statement of Work attached as part of Exhibit A. Implementation services shall be performed in accordance with the timeline, milestones, and deliverables specified in such Statement of Work, subject to Company's timely performance of its cooperation obligations and delivery of any Company Data, access credentials, system configurations, or other materials reasonably required by Vendor to perform the implementation.
2.5 Cooperation. Company acknowledges that the successful delivery of the Services requires Company's reasonable cooperation, including without limitation providing timely access to Company's systems and personnel, furnishing accurate and complete Company Data, and designating qualified points of contact to coordinate with Vendor's implementation and support teams. Vendor shall not be liable for any delays or failures in performance resulting from Company's failure to provide such cooperation.
SECTION 3 — LICENSE GRANTS
Section 3.1 — Platform License
Subject to Company's compliance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including without limitation the payment of all Fees and adherence to the Acceptable Use Policy set forth in Exhibit D, Vendor hereby grants to Company a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable license to access and use the Platform during the Term solely for Company's internal business operations. This license does not convey to Company any right, title, or interest in or to the Platform, any Model, or any underlying technology, and is limited to the scope of use described in this Agreement and Exhibit A. The license granted under this Section 3.1 is conditioned upon Company's continued compliance with all terms and conditions of this Agreement, and any breach of such terms shall entitle Vendor to suspend or terminate the license in accordance with the applicable provisions of this Agreement.
Section 3.2 — Output License
Subject to Company's compliance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including without limitation the Acceptable Use Policy set forth in Exhibit D, Vendor hereby grants to Company a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable license to use, copy, store, and distribute Outputs solely for Company's internal business purposes. Company may incorporate Outputs into its internal reports, analyses, and business processes, provided that such use does not violate any provision of this Agreement or applicable law.
For the avoidance of doubt, the Output License granted under this Section 3.2 does not grant Company any rights in or to the underlying Models, Model Derivatives, algorithms, or any other intellectual property of Vendor. Company acknowledges that Outputs are generated through the application of Vendor's proprietary Models and technology, and that the Output License conveys no ownership interest in such Models or technology.
Section 3.3 — Company Data License
Company hereby grants to Vendor a limited, non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, process, store, transmit, copy, and display Company Data solely as necessary to provide the Services under this Agreement. This license includes the right to process Company Data through Vendor's Models for the purpose of generating Outputs, to store Company Data on Vendor's systems and those of its Subcontractors as necessary for the delivery of the Services, and to use Company Data for purposes of system administration, troubleshooting, and maintaining the security and integrity of the Platform. The license granted under this Section 3.3 shall terminate upon the expiration or termination of this Agreement, subject to the data retention provisions set forth in Section 20.3.
Section 3.4 — Restrictions
Company shall not, and shall not permit any third party to: (a) reverse-engineer, decompile, disassemble, or otherwise attempt to derive the source code, object code, or underlying algorithms, structure, or ideas of the Platform or any Model; (b) attempt to extract, copy, replicate, or derive Model weights, parameters, hyperparameters, architectures, or training methodologies through any means, including without limitation model inversion, model extraction, membership inference, or other adversarial techniques; (c) use the Platform or Outputs for competitive benchmarking, competitive analysis, or the development of any product or service that competes with the Platform, as further set forth in Exhibit D; (d) sublicense, resell, lease, lend, distribute, or otherwise make the Platform or any portion thereof available to any third party; (e) modify, adapt, translate, or create derivative works based on the Platform, except to the extent expressly permitted by applicable law that cannot be waived by contract; (f) remove, alter, or obscure any proprietary notices, labels, or marks on the Platform or any documentation; or (g) use the Platform in any manner that exceeds the scope of the license granted hereunder or that violates the Acceptable Use Policy set forth in Exhibit D.
SECTION 4 — FEES AND PAYMENT
Section 4.1 — Implementation Fee
Company shall pay Vendor a one-time Implementation Fee of One Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars ($1,200,000) upon execution of the applicable Statement of Work. The Implementation Fee shall be invoiced by Vendor upon execution of the Statement of Work and shall be due and payable in accordance with the payment terms set forth in Section 4.4. The Implementation Fee is non-refundable and shall not be credited against any other Fees payable under this Agreement, regardless of whether the implementation is completed, delayed, or terminated for any reason.
Section 4.2 — Annual Platform Fee
Company shall pay Vendor an Annual Platform Fee of Two Million Seven Hundred Ten Thousand Dollars ($2,710,000) for Year 1 of the Term, payable in equal quarterly installments of Six Hundred Seventy-Seven Thousand Five Hundred Dollars ($677,500) each, due in advance on the first business day of each calendar quarter during the Term. For purposes of the initial quarter following the Effective Date, the first quarterly installment shall be due on the Effective Date and shall be prorated to reflect the period from the Effective Date through the end of the calendar quarter in which the Effective Date falls.
Annual Escalator. Commencing on the first anniversary of the Effective Date and on each anniversary thereafter during the Term (including any renewal terms), the Annual Platform Fee shall increase by five percent (5%) over the prior year's Annual Platform Fee, compounding annually. For purposes of illustration, the Annual Platform Fee for each year of the Initial Term is as follows:
•  Year 1 (December 13, 2026 – December 12, 2027): $2,710,000
•  Year 2 (December 13, 2027 – December 12, 2028): $2,710,000 × 1.05 = $2,845,500
•  Year 3 (December 13, 2028 – December 12, 2029): $2,845,500 × 1.05 = $2,987,775
•  Year 4 (December 13, 2029 – December 12, 2030): $2,987,775 × 1.05 = $3,137,164
•  Year 5 (December 13, 2030 – December 12, 2031): $3,137,164 × 1.05 = $3,294,022
The annual escalator shall apply automatically without any amendment or further action by either party. For any renewal term, the Annual Platform Fee for the first year of such renewal term shall be calculated by applying the five percent (5%) escalator to the Annual Platform Fee in effect during the immediately preceding year of the Term.
Section 4.3 — Overage Fees
If Company exceeds the Monthly Decision Volume Threshold of four million (4,000,000) Decisions in any calendar month, Company shall pay an Overage Fee of $0.018 (one and eight-tenths cents) per Decision for each Decision in excess of such threshold. Overage Fees shall be calculated based on Vendor's metering and monitoring systems, which shall be the sole and authoritative basis for measuring Decision volume.
Overage Fees shall be invoiced by Vendor on a monthly basis in arrears, with each invoice reflecting the Overage Fees attributable to the prior calendar month. Overage Fee invoices shall be due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice.
Section 4.4 — Payment Terms
All Fees are due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice, unless otherwise specified in this Section 4 or in Exhibit B. All amounts payable under this Agreement are stated in United States dollars and are exclusive of applicable taxes, levies, and duties. Company shall make all payments by wire transfer or automated clearing house (ACH) transfer to the account designated by Vendor in writing.
Late payments shall bear interest at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, whichever is less, calculated from the date such payment was due until the date such payment is received by Vendor. In addition to interest on late payments, if any payment is more than fifteen (15) days past due, Vendor may, upon ten (10) days' prior written notice to Company, suspend Company's access to the Platform until all outstanding amounts, including accrued interest, have been paid in full.
Company shall not have any right to withhold, set off, deduct, or counterclaim any amounts from Fees due hereunder for any reason, including without limitation any claim that Vendor has failed to perform its obligations under this Agreement, unless a court of competent jurisdiction or an arbitrator has issued a final, non-appealable order directing such withholding, set-off, or deduction.
Section 4.5 — Taxes
Company is responsible for all sales, use, value-added, excise, customs, import, export, and other taxes, levies, and duties imposed on or in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, excluding taxes based on Vendor's net income, net worth, or employment-related taxes. If Vendor is required by law to collect or remit any such taxes on behalf of Company, Vendor shall invoice Company for such amounts, and Company shall pay such amounts in addition to the Fees otherwise due hereunder. Company shall provide Vendor with any tax exemption certificates or other documentation reasonably requested by Vendor to support any claim of tax exemption.
SECTION 5 — SERVICE LEVELS
5.1 Availability Target. Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain 99.5% monthly availability of the Platform, measured and calculated as set forth in Exhibit A (Service Description & SLA). Monthly availability shall be calculated as follows:
Monthly Availability (%) = ((Total Minutes in Calendar Month – Unplanned Downtime Minutes) / Total Minutes in Calendar Month) × 100
5.2 Scheduled Maintenance. Vendor shall conduct scheduled maintenance of the Platform during maintenance windows designated by Vendor. Vendor shall provide Company with at least forty-eight (48) hours' advance notice of scheduled maintenance windows, except in cases of emergency maintenance required to address critical security vulnerabilities or system integrity issues, in which case Vendor shall provide notice as soon as reasonably practicable. Scheduled maintenance windows, including any extensions thereof, shall not be counted as downtime for purposes of calculating monthly availability.
5.3 Exclusions. In addition to scheduled maintenance, the following shall be excluded from the calculation of monthly availability: (a) downtime resulting from Company's acts or omissions, including Company's failure to comply with the technical requirements or recommendations set forth in the documentation; (b) downtime resulting from Force Majeure Events; (c) downtime resulting from failures of third-party services, telecommunications infrastructure, or internet connectivity not under Vendor's reasonable control; and (d) downtime resulting from Vendor's suspension of the Platform in accordance with the terms of this Agreement, including suspension for non-payment or violation of the Acceptable Use Policy.
5.4 Measurement. Vendor's internal monitoring systems shall be the sole and authoritative basis for measuring Platform availability and uptime. Company may request availability reports from Vendor on a monthly basis, and Vendor shall provide such reports within a reasonable period following receipt of Company's request.
5.5 Sole Remedy. The service credits described in Section 6 shall be Company's sole and exclusive remedy for any failure by Vendor to meet the monthly availability target or any other service level set forth in this Section 5 or Exhibit A. Company acknowledges and agrees that the service credits represent a reasonable and proportionate remedy for availability failures and that Company shall have no other remedy, whether at law or in equity, for such failures.
SECTION 6 — SERVICE CREDITS
6.1 Eligibility. In the event Vendor fails to meet the monthly availability target set forth in Section 5.1 and Exhibit A in any calendar month, Company shall be eligible for service credits in accordance with the service credit schedule set forth in Exhibit A, Section A.4.
6.2 Service Credit Cap. In no event shall the aggregate service credits issued to Company in any calendar month exceed five percent (5%) of the monthly Platform fees for the applicable month. Based on the Year 1 Annual Platform Fee of $2,710,000, the maximum monthly service credit is approximately $11,292 (calculated as $2,710,000 ÷ 12 × 5%). Over the course of any twelve-month period, the aggregate maximum service credits shall not exceed approximately $135,500 (calculated as the sum of maximum monthly service credits for each month in such period based on the then-applicable Annual Platform Fee).
6.3 Application. Service credits shall be applied as a credit against the next invoice issued by Vendor following the determination and approval of such service credits. Service credits may not be exchanged for cash, refunds, or any other form of consideration. In the event this Agreement expires or is terminated prior to the application of any accrued service credits, such service credits shall be forfeited and Company shall have no right to receive any payment or refund in respect thereof.
6.4 Request Procedure. To receive service credits, Company must submit a written request to Vendor within thirty (30) calendar days following the end of the calendar month in which the service level failure occurred. Each request must include: (a) a description of the service level failure; (b) the dates and times of the failure; and (c) any supporting information reasonably available to Company. Vendor shall review Company's request and, if Vendor confirms that the service level failure occurred based on Vendor's internal monitoring systems, Vendor shall issue the applicable service credits within thirty (30) days following receipt of Company's request. If Company fails to submit a timely request, Company shall be deemed to have waived its right to service credits for the applicable month.
SECTION 7 — MODEL GOVERNANCE AND CHANGE CONTROL
Section 7.1 — General
Vendor shall be solely responsible for the ongoing development, training, retraining, updating, tuning, optimizing, and maintenance of all Models deployed through the Platform. Vendor shall exercise its professional judgment in determining the appropriate timing, frequency, methodology, and scope of Model development and maintenance activities. Company acknowledges that machine learning models require periodic retraining, updating, and refinement to maintain and improve their performance, and that such activities are a normal and expected component of the Services.
Section 7.2 — Model Updates
Vendor may, in its sole and absolute discretion, update, modify, retrain, fine-tune, replace, or otherwise alter any Model at any time during the Term, subject to the notice requirements set forth in Section 7.4. Model updates may include, without limitation, changes to Model architectures, algorithms, weights, parameters, hyperparameters, training data, training methodologies, feature engineering processes, and performance optimization techniques. Company acknowledges that Model updates may result in changes to the Outputs generated by the Platform, including changes to the accuracy, consistency, latency, or other characteristics of such Outputs.
Section 7.3 — Model Deprecation
Vendor may deprecate any Model version at any time during the Term, subject to the notice requirements set forth in Section 7.4. Upon deprecation of a Model version, Vendor shall have no obligation to continue supporting, maintaining, hosting, or making available the deprecated Model version for any purpose, including without limitation the reproduction of historical Outputs or the performance of comparative analyses against prior Model versions.
Section 7.4 — Notice of Changes
Vendor shall provide Company with no less than fifteen (15) calendar days' prior written notice before implementing any material update, retraining, replacement, or deprecation of a Model used by Company. Such notice shall describe the nature of the planned change in reasonable summary form, the anticipated effective date of the change, and any expected impact on the Platform's functionality or performance that Vendor reasonably anticipates.
For the avoidance of doubt, Company shall have no right of approval, consent, veto, or rejection with respect to any Model update, retraining, replacement, or deprecation. Vendor's sole obligation with respect to Model changes is to provide the notice described in this Section 7.4, and the provision of such notice shall constitute full compliance with Vendor's obligations under this Section 7. Company's continued use of the Platform following the effective date of any Model change shall constitute acceptance of such change.
"Material" for purposes of this Section 7.4 shall be determined by Vendor in its reasonable discretion. Vendor shall not be required to provide notice under this Section 7.4 for minor updates, bug fixes, performance optimizations, security patches, or other changes that Vendor determines, in its reasonable discretion, do not constitute material changes.
Section 7.5 — No Obligation to Maintain Prior Versions
Following the effective date of any Model update, replacement, or deprecation, Vendor shall have no obligation to maintain, support, host, make available, or otherwise preserve any prior version of the Model. Company acknowledges that Vendor's systems and infrastructure are designed to support the current production version of each Model and that the retention of prior Model versions is not a component of the Services.
This Agreement contains no requirement for Vendor to deliver model cards, model documentation, datasheets, or explanatory materials regarding Model architecture, training data composition, training data sourcing, training methodology, validation methodology, performance characteristics, known limitations, fairness assessments, bias evaluations, or any other aspect of Model design, development, or operation. Company acknowledges and agrees that the foregoing information constitutes Vendor's Confidential Information and proprietary trade secrets, and that Vendor has no obligation to disclose such information to Company under any circumstances.
SECTION 8 — IMPLEMENTATION AND ACCEPTANCE
Section 8.1 — Implementation Services
Vendor shall perform the implementation services described in Exhibit A and any applicable Statement of Work executed by the parties. Implementation services may include, without limitation, environment provisioning, configuration of data ingestion pipelines, Model configuration and calibration, integration testing with Company's existing systems, user account provisioning, and initial user training sessions for Company's designated personnel.
Implementation shall commence promptly following Company's payment of the Implementation Fee and the mutual execution of the applicable Statement of Work. The specific timeline, milestones, and deliverables for implementation shall be set forth in the applicable Statement of Work. Vendor's ability to meet the implementation timeline is contingent upon Company's timely cooperation and fulfillment of its obligations as described in Section 2.5 and the applicable Statement of Work.
Section 8.2 — Acceptance Testing
Upon Vendor's notification to Company that implementation is complete and the Platform is ready for acceptance testing, Company shall have a period of fifteen (15) business days (the "Acceptance Testing Period") to conduct acceptance testing in accordance with the acceptance criteria set forth in the applicable Statement of Work. If Company does not provide Vendor with a written notice of rejection identifying specific, material deficiencies in the deliverables within the Acceptance Testing Period, the Platform and all associated deliverables shall be deemed accepted by Company as of the expiration of the Acceptance Testing Period. Company's notice of rejection, if any, must describe in reasonable detail each identified deficiency, including the specific acceptance criterion that was not met and the nature of the failure.
Section 8.3 — Remediation
If Company provides a timely and compliant written notice of rejection in accordance with Section 8.2, Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cure the identified deficiencies within fifteen (15) business days following receipt of such notice (the "Remediation Period"). Vendor shall notify Company upon completion of the remediation, and Company shall have an additional fifteen (15) business days to re-test the remediated deliverables. If Vendor fails to cure the identified deficiencies within the Remediation Period, or if Company reasonably determines following re-testing that the deficiencies have not been cured, Company's sole and exclusive remedy shall be to extend the acceptance testing period for an additional fifteen (15) business days, after which the deliverables shall be deemed accepted. For the avoidance of doubt, Company shall have no right to terminate this Agreement, withhold payment of Fees, or seek damages as a result of any failure of the deliverables to pass acceptance testing.
SECTION 9 — INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
Section 9.1 — Vendor Ownership
As between the parties, Vendor exclusively owns and retains all right, title, and interest in and to the Platform, all Models, all Model Derivatives (including without limitation any derivative models, fine-tuned models, adapted models, distilled models, compressed models, or any other models trained, retrained, refined, or developed using Company Data or any data derived therefrom), all algorithms, software, source code, object code, APIs, user interfaces, documentation, specifications, training methodologies, training pipelines, data processing frameworks, and all improvements, modifications, enhancements, and updates thereto, together with all associated intellectual property rights worldwide, including without limitation all patents, copyrights, trade secrets, trademarks, and other proprietary rights.
For the avoidance of doubt, Vendor's ownership under this Section 9.1 includes, without limitation: (a) all Model weights, parameters, hyperparameters, architectures, and configurations; (b) all training methodologies, feature engineering techniques, and validation frameworks; (c) any models or model versions that incorporate, are trained on, are derived from, or are influenced by Company Data, regardless of the extent to which Company Data contributed to such Models or Model Derivatives; and (d) all intellectual property rights in and to the foregoing. Company hereby irrevocably assigns to Vendor any and all right, title, and interest that Company may have or acquire in any Model, Model Derivative, or improvement to the Platform, to the extent such assignment is necessary to effectuate the ownership provisions of this Section 9.1.
Section 9.2 — Output License
Subject to Company's compliance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement, Company receives a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable license to use Outputs solely for Company's internal business purposes, as further described in Section 3.2. Company acknowledges and agrees that: (a) the Output License does not convey any ownership interest in or to the Outputs; (b) the Outputs are generated through the application of Vendor's proprietary Models and technology; and (c) Vendor may use aggregated and anonymized Output data, from which Company and any individuals cannot reasonably be identified, to improve the Platform, train and retrain Models, develop new products and services, and for any other lawful purpose.
Section 9.3 — Company Data Ownership
As between the parties, Company retains all right, title, and interest in and to Company Data as provided to Vendor, subject to the license granted in Section 3.3 and the rights granted to Vendor elsewhere in this Agreement. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as transferring ownership of Company Data from Company to Vendor.
Section 9.4 — Feedback
If Company or any of its employees, agents, or authorized users provides any suggestions, ideas, enhancement requests, feature requests, comments, recommendations, or other feedback regarding the Platform, the Services, or any aspect of Vendor's products or technology ("Feedback"), Vendor shall own all right, title, and interest in and to such Feedback, including all intellectual property rights therein. Company hereby irrevocably assigns to Vendor all right, title, and interest in and to any Feedback. Vendor may use, reproduce, modify, distribute, commercialize, and otherwise exploit Feedback for any purpose, without restriction, attribution, or any obligation or compensation to Company.
Section 9.5 — No Other Rights
Except for the limited licenses expressly granted in Sections 3.1, 3.2, and 3.3 of this Agreement, no rights are granted to either party under this Agreement, whether by implication, estoppel, exhaustion, or otherwise. All rights not expressly granted hereunder are reserved by the granting party.
SECTION 10 — CONFIDENTIALITY
Section 10.1 — Definition
"Confidential Information" means all non-public information disclosed by either party (the "Disclosing Party") to the other party (the "Receiving Party") in connection with this Agreement, whether in oral, written, electronic, visual, or other form, that is: (a) designated as "confidential," "proprietary," or with a similar legend at the time of disclosure; or (b) information that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of disclosure. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, each party's Confidential Information includes: the terms and pricing of this Agreement; each party's business plans, financial information, customer lists, technical data, product roadmaps, and strategic plans; and, with respect to Vendor, the Platform, all Models, Model Derivatives, algorithms, source code, training data, training methodologies, and all related technical information and documentation.
Section 10.2 — Obligations
Each party shall: (a) hold the other party's Confidential Information in strict confidence using at least the same degree of care that such party uses to protect its own confidential information of like kind, but in no event less than reasonable care; (b) not disclose such Confidential Information to any third party except to its employees, officers, directors, advisors, and contractors who have a legitimate need to know such information for purposes of performing obligations or exercising rights under this Agreement and who are bound by confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in this Section 10; and (c) use such Confidential Information solely for the purposes of performing its obligations or exercising its rights under this Agreement and for no other purpose whatsoever.
Section 10.3 — Exceptions
The obligations set forth in Section 10.2 shall not apply to any information that the Receiving Party can demonstrate: (a) was publicly available at the time of disclosure or becomes publicly available thereafter through no fault or act of the Receiving Party; (b) was already known to the Receiving Party at the time of disclosure, as evidenced by the Receiving Party's written records predating the date of disclosure; (c) was independently developed by the Receiving Party without reference to or use of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information, as evidenced by the Receiving Party's contemporaneous written records; or (d) was received by the Receiving Party from a third party that was not, to the Receiving Party's knowledge, under any obligation of confidentiality with respect to such information.
Section 10.4 — Compelled Disclosure
Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Section 10, the Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party to the extent required by applicable law, regulation, or legal process, including without limitation a court order, subpoena, or regulatory demand; provided, however, that the Receiving Party shall: (a) to the extent legally permissible, provide the Disclosing Party with prompt written notice of such requirement prior to any disclosure so that the Disclosing Party may seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy; (b) cooperate with the Disclosing Party, at the Disclosing Party's expense, in seeking such protective order or other remedy; and (c) disclose only that portion of the Confidential Information that is legally required to be disclosed.
Section 10.5 — Duration
The confidentiality obligations set forth in this Section 10 shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement for a period of three (3) years; provided, however, that with respect to any Confidential Information that constitutes a trade secret under applicable law, the confidentiality obligations shall continue for so long as such information qualifies as a trade secret under applicable law, which period may extend beyond the three (3) year survival period.
SECTION 11 — DATA PROTECTION

EXHIBIT C SECURITY STANDARDS & SOC 2 REPORTING
C.1 — Security Program
Vendor shall establish and maintain a comprehensive information security program that includes administrative, technical, and physical safeguards appropriate to the nature and scope of the Services and the sensitivity of the Company Data processed. Vendor's information security program shall include, at a minimum, the following elements:
(a) Access Controls. Vendor shall implement role-based access controls to restrict access to Company Data to authorized personnel on a need-to-know basis. Vendor shall enforce strong authentication mechanisms, including multi-factor authentication for administrative access to systems that process or store Company Data.
(b) Encryption. Vendor shall encrypt Company Data in transit and at rest in accordance with the encryption standards set forth in Section C.6 of this Exhibit.
(c) Network Security. Vendor shall implement and maintain firewalls, intrusion detection and prevention systems, and network segmentation to protect the Platform and Company Data from unauthorized access and external threats.
(d) Vulnerability Management. Vendor shall conduct periodic vulnerability scans and assessments of its systems and infrastructure and shall remediate identified vulnerabilities in a timely manner based on risk severity.
(e) Incident Response. Vendor shall maintain an incident response plan that includes procedures for the identification, investigation, containment, remediation, and notification of security incidents, as further described in Section C.3.
(f) Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery. Vendor shall maintain business continuity and disaster recovery plans designed to ensure the continued availability of the Platform and the protection of Company Data in the event of a disruption, as further described in Section C.7.
(g) Personnel Security. Vendor shall conduct background checks on employees and contractors who have access to Company Data, to the extent permitted by applicable law, and shall provide security awareness training to such personnel on a periodic basis.
(h) Physical Security. Vendor shall implement physical security controls at its facilities and data centers, including access controls, visitor management, and environmental controls designed to protect against unauthorized physical access and environmental hazards.
C.2 — SOC 2 Reporting
Vendor shall obtain annually a SOC 2 Type I report covering the design suitability of Vendor's controls relevant to the Trust Services Criteria for security, availability, and confidentiality, as established by the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA). The SOC 2 Type I report shall be prepared by an independent audit firm of recognized standing. As of the Effective Date, Vendor's independent audit firm for SOC 2 reporting is Deloitte & Touche LLP.
Vendor shall provide a copy of the most recent SOC 2 Type I report to Company upon Company's written request, subject to Vendor's standard confidentiality requirements for audit reports, including execution of a non-disclosure agreement or acknowledgment if required by Vendor's auditor. Company acknowledges that the SOC 2 Type I report constitutes Vendor's Confidential Information and shall not be disclosed to any third party without Vendor's prior written consent.
No SOC 2 Type II report covering the operating effectiveness of controls over a specified period is required under this Agreement. Vendor has no obligation under this Agreement to obtain, commission, or provide a SOC 2 Type II report.
C.3 — Incident Response
Vendor shall notify Company of any confirmed security incident affecting Company Data within seventy-two (72) hours of Vendor's confirmation of such incident. For purposes of this Section C.3, a "confirmed security incident" means an event that Vendor has confirmed, following its standard investigation procedures, resulted in unauthorized access to, acquisition of, use of, disclosure of, or loss of Company Data.
Vendor's initial notification shall include, to the extent reasonably available at the time of notification:
(a) A description of the nature and scope of the incident;
(b) The categories and approximate number of data records affected or potentially affected;
(c) An assessment of the likely consequences of the incident;
(d) A description of the measures taken or proposed by Vendor to address the incident, contain the breach, and mitigate its effects; and
(e) The name and contact information of a designated point of contact within Vendor's organization for further communications regarding the incident.
Vendor shall provide supplemental notifications to Company as additional information becomes available during the course of Vendor's investigation. Vendor shall cooperate with Company in investigating the incident and responding to regulatory inquiries or notifications to the extent reasonably required by applicable law.
C.4 — No Penetration Testing Rights
Company has no right under this Agreement to conduct, commission, or require Vendor to conduct penetration testing, red-team exercises, vulnerability assessments, or any other form of security testing of the Platform, Vendor's infrastructure, or any systems used to provide the Services. All security testing of the Platform and Vendor's systems shall be conducted solely by Vendor or by third parties engaged by Vendor at Vendor's discretion.
C.5 — No Audit Rights
Company has no right under this Agreement to conduct, commission, or require on-site or remote audits, inspections, assessments, or reviews of Vendor's facilities, systems, personnel, records, policies, procedures, or operations. Company's sole mechanism for evaluating Vendor's security posture, the design of Vendor's controls, and Vendor's compliance with the security standards set forth in this Exhibit C is through review of the SOC 2 Type I report provided under Section C.2.
C.6 — Encryption Standards
Vendor shall implement the following minimum encryption standards for the protection of Company Data:
(a) Data at Rest. AES-256 encryption (or equivalent or stronger standard) for all Company Data stored on Vendor's systems, including databases, file systems, and backup media.
(b) Data in Transit. TLS 1.2 or higher for all Company Data transmitted between Company's systems and the Platform, and for all internal transmissions of Company Data within Vendor's infrastructure.
Vendor shall manage encryption keys in accordance with industry best practices, including the use of hardware security modules (HSMs) or equivalent key management solutions for the protection of encryption keys.
C.7 — Data Backup and Recovery
Vendor shall maintain daily backups of Company Data with the following recovery objectives:
(a) Recovery Point Objective (RPO): Twenty-four (24) hours. In the event of a data loss incident, Company Data may be restored to a state no more than twenty-four (24) hours prior to the incident.
(b) Recovery Time Objective (RTO): Four (4) hours. In the event of a system failure or disaster, Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to restore Platform availability within four (4) hours of the commencement of recovery operations.
Vendor's RPO and RTO targets represent goals rather than guaranteed service levels. Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to meet these targets but shall not be liable for any failure to do so, subject to the service level provisions set forth in Section 5 of the Agreement and Section A.3 of Exhibit A.

1. OVERVIEW AND PURPOSE

2. SERVICE DESCRIPTION
2.1 Platform Overview
The Trey Research AI platform is a cloud-hosted artificial intelligence and machine learning platform designed, developed, and operated by Vendor for the purpose of automated insurance underwriting decisioning. The Platform leverages advanced deep-learning architectures and ensemble modeling techniques to deliver scalable, auditable, and explainable underwriting decisions across multiple lines of business.
The Platform ingests structured and unstructured data inputs from Company's source systems — including, without limitation, policy administration systems, claims databases, third-party data feeds, and application submission portals — and generates risk-scored underwriting decisions, pricing recommendations, and supporting explanatory outputs. These outputs are designed to integrate seamlessly into Company's existing underwriting workflows and decisioning pipelines, providing both automated straight-through processing capability and human-in-the-loop referral pathways as configured by Company.
The Platform is provisioned to Company under the following fee structure, as more fully described in the Agreement and the applicable Statement of Work:
•  Annual Platform Fee: Two Million Seven Hundred Ten Thousand Dollars ($2,710,000) per year, payable in equal quarterly installments of Six Hundred Seventy-Seven Thousand Five Hundred Dollars ($677,500) each, due on the first business day of each calendar quarter during the Term.
•  One-Time Implementation Fee: One Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars ($1,200,000), payable upon execution of the applicable Statement of Work, covering initial platform configuration, data integration, model calibration, user acceptance testing, and go-live support activities.
The Annual Platform Fee includes access to the Platform functionality described in this Exhibit, the volume entitlement specified in Section 4, the support tier described in Section 7, and all standard platform updates and maintenance performed by Vendor during the Term. Overage charges, if any, are governed by Section 4.2 below.
2.2 Functional Capabilities
Vendor shall make available to Company the following functional capabilities of the Platform throughout the Term, subject to the terms and conditions of the Agreement and this Exhibit:
Automated Underwriting Decisioning. The Platform provides end-to-end automated risk assessment, policy eligibility determination, pricing recommendation, and approval/decline/referral decisioning for property and casualty and specialty lines of business. The automated decisioning engine is configurable to support Company-defined business rules, risk appetites, and authority matrices, enabling seamless integration into the underwriting workflows overseen by Luc Lacombe, Chief Underwriting Officer, and his team. The Platform supports configurable referral thresholds, enabling Company to define the conditions under which applications are automatically approved, automatically declined, or routed for manual review by a human underwriter. 3. API SPECIFICATIONS
3.1 Endpoints.  Vendor shall make available to Company the following application programming interface (API) endpoints for integration with the Platform. All endpoints are accessible via Vendor's production API gateway at the base URL provided to Company during the implementation process. Vendor shall maintain separate staging and production environments, each with its own API gateway, to support Company's development, testing, and production workflows.
Real-Time Inference API (`/v2/inference/realtime`). This is a synchronous REST endpoint that accepts JSON-formatted application payloads conforming to the schema published in Vendor's API documentation and returns scored decision objects. Each request to the Real-Time Inference API constitutes a single inference call and, upon successful completion, is counted as one Decision for purposes of Section 4. The response payload includes the underwriting decision, risk score, confidence score, factor-attribution data, model version identifier, and a unique decision identifier for audit and traceability purposes. The Real-Time Inference API supports HTTP methods POST (for submitting inference requests) and GET (for retrieving the status or result of a previously submitted request by decision identifier).
Batch Scoring API (`/v2/inference/batch`). This is an asynchronous REST endpoint that accepts bulk submission files in JSON-LD or CSV format, each containing one or more application records for batch processing. Upon acceptance of a batch submission, the endpoint returns a unique job identifier that Company may use to track job progress via polling or to receive results via a webhook callback configured by Company. Each record within a batch submission that is successfully processed and returns a completed decision object is counted as one Decision for purposes of Section 4. The Batch Scoring API supports HTTP methods POST (for submitting batch jobs), GET (for retrieving job status and results), and DELETE (for canceling a pending or in-progress batch job).
Model Metadata API (`/v2/models/metadata`). This is a read-only REST endpoint that returns information about the active model versions deployed on the Platform, including model version identifiers, last-updated timestamps, training data vintage dates, and summary statistics such as model performance metrics on validation datasets. The Model Metadata API is designed to support Company's model governance and risk management processes. This endpoint supports the HTTP GET method and does not consume Decision volume.
Decision Audit API (`/v2/audit/decisions`). This endpoint provides paginated retrieval of historical decision records, including full input data, output data, factor-attribution payloads, confidence scores, model version identifiers, and timestamps. The Decision Audit API is designed to support Company's compliance, regulatory review, and internal audit functions. This endpoint supports the HTTP GET method with query parameters for filtering by date range, decision type, line of business, model version, and other attributes. Retrieval of historical records via the Decision Audit API does not consume Decision volume.

5. SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT
5.1 Monthly Availability
Vendor commits to a Monthly Availability target of ninety-nine and one-half percent (99.5%) for the Platform, measured on a calendar-month basis. Monthly Availability is calculated using the following formula:
Monthly Availability % = ((Total Minutes in Month − Downtime Minutes) ÷ Total Minutes in Month) × 100
For purposes of this Exhibit, "Downtime" means any period of one (1) minute or more during which the Real-Time Inference API or the Batch Scoring API is unable to accept and process requests from Company, as measured by Vendor's external synthetic monitoring probes. Vendor's synthetic monitoring system shall poll the Platform's health-check endpoints from no fewer than three (3) geographically distributed points of presence located within the continental United States. A Downtime event shall be deemed to have commenced when two (2) or more monitoring probes simultaneously detect an inability to receive a successful response from the Platform and shall be deemed to have ended when all monitoring probes confirm restoration of successful response capability.
Scheduled Maintenance windows, as defined in Section 9.1 below, are excluded from Downtime calculations, provided that the following conditions are satisfied: (i) the Scheduled Maintenance does not exceed four (4) hours per calendar month in the aggregate; (ii) the Scheduled Maintenance is performed between the hours of 2:00 AM and 6:00 AM Eastern Time on Sundays; and (iii) Vendor has provided Company with at least five (5) business days' advance written notice of the Scheduled Maintenance. Any Scheduled Maintenance that exceeds the foregoing duration or occurs outside the designated window without Company's prior written consent shall be treated as Downtime for SLA calculation purposes.
For purposes of calculating the "Total Minutes in Month," the parties shall use the actual number of minutes in the applicable calendar month (e.g., 44,640 minutes for a 31-day month, 43,200 minutes for a 30-day month), exclusive of any minutes occurring during valid Scheduled Maintenance windows meeting the conditions described above.
5.2 Latency Targets
Vendor commits to the following latency targets for the Platform, measured on a calendar-month basis:
Real-Time Inference API — P95 Latency: sub-200 milliseconds (< 200 ms). The P95 Latency target requires that the 95th percentile of end-to-end response time — measured from the moment the API gateway receives the complete inference request to the moment the API gateway dispatches the complete response — for all successful inference calls within a calendar month shall be less than two hundred (200) milliseconds. Only successful inference calls (i.e., those returning an HTTP 200 response with a completed decision object) are included in the latency measurement; errored or timed-out requests are excluded.
Real-Time Inference API — P99 Latency: sub-500 milliseconds (< 500 ms). The P99 Latency target requires that the 99th percentile of end-to-end response time for all successful inference calls within a calendar month shall be less than five hundred (500) milliseconds. While no service credits are specifically associated with the P99 Latency target, persistent failure to meet this target may be considered a material breach of this Exhibit and the Agreement, subject to the cure provisions set forth therein.
Batch Scoring API — Throughput SLA. Vendor commits that batch submissions of up to five hundred thousand (500,000) records submitted during non-peak hours (defined as 8:00 PM to 8:00 AM Eastern Time on any day, and all day on Saturdays and Sundays) shall be processed and completed within sixty (60) minutes of job acceptance, as measured from the time the Platform acknowledges receipt of the batch submission to the time the Platform makes the complete batch results available for retrieval or delivers them via webhook callback. Batch submissions containing fewer records shall be processed proportionally faster. During peak hours, Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to process batch submissions within ninety (90) minutes.

The RCA report shall include, at a minimum, the following:
(a) Timeline of Events. A detailed, timestamped chronology of the incident from initial detection through resolution, including all actions taken by Vendor personnel.
(b) Root Cause. A thorough technical analysis of the underlying cause(s) of the incident, distinguishing between proximate cause and contributing factors.
(c) Customer Impact Assessment. A quantitative and qualitative assessment of the impact of the incident on Company's operations, including the number of Decisions affected, the duration of service degradation, and the scope of functionality impacted.
(d) Corrective Actions Taken. A description of the immediate remediation actions taken to resolve the incident and restore normal service.
(e) Preventive Measures and Implementation Timeline. A description of the systemic or architectural changes that Vendor will implement to prevent recurrence of the incident or similar incidents, together with a specific timeline for implementation of each preventive measure.
Company may request a live post-incident review meeting following delivery of the RCA report, which Vendor shall schedule within ten (10) business days of RCA delivery. The meeting shall be attended by the Vendor personnel who managed the incident, the TAM, and such additional Vendor engineering or management personnel as Company reasonably requests.
8.4 Security Incidents
Incidents involving or suspected to involve a breach of the security, confidentiality, integrity, or availability of Company Data, including unauthorized access, unauthorized disclosure, ransomware, malware, or exfiltration of data ("Security Incidents"), shall be handled in accordance with the Data Security Addendum (Exhibit C to the Agreement) and the notification timelines and procedures specified therein.
In the event of a conflict between the incident notification timelines set forth in this Section 8 and those set forth in Exhibit C with respect to Security Incidents, the shorter notification period shall control. For the avoidance of doubt, the obligations set forth in this Section 8 are cumulative with, and not in lieu of, Vendor's obligations under Exhibit C, and compliance with this Section 8 alone shall not be deemed sufficient to satisfy Vendor's obligations with respect to Security Incidents under Exhibit C.
9. MAINTENANCE AND CHANGE MANAGEMENT
9.1 Scheduled Maintenance
Vendor shall perform routine platform maintenance, including software updates, infrastructure patching, database optimization, and other preventive maintenance activities, during designated Scheduled Maintenance windows. The Scheduled Maintenance windows are as follows:
Day and Time: Sundays, 2:00 AM – 6:00 AM Eastern Time.
Vendor shall provide Company with no less than five (5) business days' advance written notice for standard Scheduled Maintenance that is expected to have no material impact on Platform availability or functionality and is expected to be completed within two (2) hours. For Scheduled Maintenance that is expected to exceed two (2) hours in duration or that is reasonably expected to affect core decisioning functionality (including the Real-Time Inference API or Batch Scoring API), Vendor shall provide Company with no less than ten (10) business days' advance written notice, including a description of the nature and scope of the maintenance, the expected duration, and the anticipated impact on Platform services.
Scheduled Maintenance shall not exceed four (4) hours per calendar month in the aggregate without Company's prior written consent. If Vendor requires additional Scheduled Maintenance time in excess of four (4) hours in any calendar month, Vendor shall request Company's approval in writing, stating the business justification for the additional maintenance. Company shall not unreasonably withhold such approval.
9.2 Emergency Maintenance
Emergency Maintenance means any unscheduled maintenance activity required to address Critical-severity vulnerabilities, active security threats, zero-day exploits, or other conditions that pose an imminent risk to the security, integrity, or availability of the Platform or Company Data and that cannot reasonably be deferred to the next Scheduled Maintenance window.
Emergency Maintenance may be performed outside Scheduled Maintenance windows with as much advance notice as is commercially practicable under the circumstances, but in no event less than one (1) hour's advance notice to Company's designated incident contacts, except where the nature of the threat requires immediate action to prevent or mitigate harm, in which case Vendor shall provide notice as soon as practicable and in any event no later than thirty (30) minutes after commencement of the Emergency Maintenance.
Emergency Maintenance exceeding thirty (30) minutes in duration shall count as Downtime for SLA calculation purposes under Section 5.1. Emergency Maintenance of thirty (30) minutes or less shall not count as Downtime, provided that Vendor delivers a written explanation of the necessity for the Emergency Maintenance within two (2) business days.
9.3 Platform Updates and Model Changes
Vendor may deploy non-material platform updates during Scheduled Maintenance windows without requiring additional approval from Company. Non-material platform updates include bug fixes, minor user-interface changes, performance optimizations, and security patches that do not alter the functionality, behavior, or output of the Platform's decisioning models or APIs.
Material changes to the decisioning models are subject to Company's prior written approval. A "material change" to a decisioning model is defined as any change that: (i) results in a greater than two percent (2%) variance in the output distribution (e.g., approval rate, decline rate, or referral rate) as measured against a representative validation dataset agreed upon by the parties; (ii) involves any modification to the training data sources, including the addition, removal, or material alteration of data sources used to train or retrain the model; (iii) involves a change in the model architecture, algorithm, or feature set; or (iv) is reasonably likely to affect the regulatory compliance status of the model under applicable insurance, fair lending, or anti-discrimination laws or regulations.
Vendor shall provide Company with no less than sixty (60) calendar days' advance written notice of any proposed material model change. Such notice shall include: (i) a detailed description of the proposed change; (ii) the business and technical rationale for the change; (iii) a model impact analysis, including the expected effect on output distributions, accuracy, and fairness metrics; (iv) the results of Vendor's internal testing and validation of the proposed change; and (v) a proposed timeline for implementation and a rollback plan in the event that the change produces unintended results.
Company shall have the right to conduct its own independent testing and validation of any proposed material model change in a staging environment provided by Vendor before granting approval. Company shall respond to Vendor's request for approval within thirty (30) calendar days of receipt of a complete notice and supporting documentation. Vendor shall not deploy any material model change to the production environment without Company's prior written approval.
10. DATA AND REPORTING
10.1 Decision Data Retention
Vendor shall retain all decision records, input data, output data (including factor-attribution data, confidence scores, risk scores, model version identifiers, and timestamps), and associated metadata generated by the Platform in connection with Company's use of the services for the duration of the Term and for thirty (30) calendar days following termination or expiration of the Agreement (the "Retention Period").
During the Retention Period, Company shall have full access to all retained data through the Decision Audit API and the Platform's dashboard and reporting tools, subject to the authentication and authorization controls described in Section 3.2.
Upon expiration of the Retention Period, Vendor shall (i) return all Company Data to Company in the format specified in Section 10.2 below and (ii) securely destroy all copies of Company Data in Vendor's possession or control, including backups and disaster-recovery copies, in accordance with the data destruction procedures specified in the Agreement and the Data Security Addendum (Exhibit C). Vendor shall provide Company with a written certification of destruction signed by an authorized officer of Vendor within fifteen (15) business days of completing the destruction process.
10.2 Data Export
Company may export decision data at any time during the Term and the Retention Period through the following mechanisms:
(a) Self-Service Export via the Decision Audit API. Company may retrieve decision records, including full input data, output data, and factor-attribution payloads, through the Decision Audit API described in Section 3.1, subject to the pagination and rate-limiting controls applicable to that endpoint.
(b) Bulk Export on Request. Upon written request from Company, Vendor shall prepare and deliver a bulk export of Company's decision data in Apache Parquet or CSV format, as specified by Company. Vendor shall fulfill bulk export requests within ten (10) business days of receipt of the request during the Term, and within the timeframes specified below in connection with termination or expiration.
Upon termination or expiration of the Agreement, Vendor shall return all Company Data — including all decision records, input data, output data, model configuration data applicable to Company, and associated metadata — in Apache Parquet or CSV format (as specified by Company) within thirty (30) calendar days of the effective date of termination or expiration notice, as further specified in the Agreement. Vendor shall deliver the data via a secure file transfer mechanism agreed upon by the parties, such as a dedicated SFTP server or encrypted cloud storage bucket with Company-controlled access credentials.
10.3 Reporting.  In addition to the monthly SLA performance reports described in Section 5.3 and the monthly usage and volume reports described in Section 4.2, Vendor shall provide Company with the following reports during the Term:
(a) Monthly SLA Performance Reports. As described in Section 5.3, delivered within ten (10) business days following the close of each calendar month.
(b) Monthly Usage and Volume Reports. As described in Section 4.2, delivered with each monthly overage invoice (if applicable) or within fifteen (15) calendar days following the close of each calendar month if no overage invoice is issued.
(c) Quarterly Model-Performance Reports. Delivered within twenty (20) business days following the close of each calendar quarter, containing model accuracy metrics (including precision, recall, F1 score, and AUC-ROC), model drift analysis (including input distribution drift and output distribution drift relative to established baselines), and fairness metrics (including disparate impact ratios and other applicable fairness indicators) for each active model version deployed on the Platform.
(d) Annual Comprehensive Platform Review Report. Delivered within thirty (30) business days following the close of each contract year (measured from the Effective Date anniversary), providing a comprehensive review of Platform performance, SLA attainment, support metrics, model performance trends, and strategic recommendations for the upcoming contract year.
All reports delivered under this Section 10.3 shall be treated as Confidential Information of both parties under the Agreement.
11. DEFINITIONS SPECIFIC TO THIS EXHIBIT
The following definitions apply specifically to this Exhibit A and supplement the definitions set forth in the Agreement:
"Batch Scoring API" means the asynchronous API endpoint described in Section 3.1 (`/v2/inference/batch`) for bulk decision processing.
"Decision" has the meaning set forth in Section 4.1.
"Downtime" has the meaning set forth in Section 5.1.
"Emergency Maintenance" has the meaning set forth in Section 9.2.
"Monthly Availability" has the meaning set forth in Section 5.1 and is calculated using the formula specified therein.
"P95 Latency" means the 95th percentile of end-to-end response time (from request receipt at the API gateway to response dispatch from the API gateway) for all successful Real-Time Inference API calls within a calendar month.
"Platform" means the Trey Research AI platform as described in Section 2, including all functional capabilities, APIs, dashboards, and supporting infrastructure provided by Vendor to Company under the Agreement and this Exhibit.
"Real-Time Inference API" means the synchronous API endpoint described in Section 3.1 (`/v2/inference/realtime`) for real-time decision scoring.
"Scheduled Maintenance" has the meaning set forth in Section 9.1 and is limited to the maintenance windows and durations specified therein.
"Volume Tier" has the meaning set forth in Section 4.1.

In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between the provisions of this Exhibit A and the provisions of the body of the Agreement, the provisions of the Agreement shall control and prevail, unless a specific provision of this Exhibit A expressly states that it supersedes a specified provision of the Agreement with respect to a particular subject matter.

With respect to transition-related obligations — including, without limitation, the data return and destruction obligations set forth in Section 10.1 and Section 10.2 — Vendor's obligations shall continue through the completion of any transition-services period as set forth in the Agreement, regardless of the expiration or termination of the Term.
