EXHIBIT C
SECURITY STANDARDS & SOC 2 REPORTING
to the Trey Research Vendor Agreement v.4.2
Doc ID: TR-EA-2026-0417
This Exhibit C (this "Exhibit") is attached to and incorporated into the Trey Research Vendor Agreement v.4.2 (the "Agreement") by and between Trey Research, a Delaware corporation ("Vendor"), and the customer identified in the Agreement ("Customer"). Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Exhibit have the meanings given to them in the Agreement. In the event of any conflict between this Exhibit and the body of the Agreement, the terms of the Agreement shall control unless this Exhibit expressly states otherwise.
1. OVERVIEW AND SCOPE
This Exhibit establishes the minimum information-security standards, reporting obligations, and data-handling procedures that Vendor shall establish, implement, and maintain throughout the Term with respect to the Platform and all Customer Data processed thereunder. The standards set forth herein are intended to ensure that Vendor maintains reasonable and appropriate safeguards commensurate with the sensitivity of Customer Data and the nature of the services provided under the Agreement.
The scope of this Exhibit covers all environments—including, without limitation, production, staging, quality-assurance, development (to the extent Customer Data is present), and disaster-recovery environments—in which Customer Data is stored, processed, transmitted, or otherwise handled by Vendor, its affiliates, or its authorized subcontractors. For the avoidance of doubt, to the extent that any subcontractor engaged by Vendor pursuant to the Agreement processes, stores, or transmits Customer Data, Vendor shall ensure that such subcontractor adheres to standards that are no less protective than those set forth in this Exhibit, and Vendor shall remain fully responsible to Customer for any acts or omissions of such subcontractors.
2. INFORMATION SECURITY PROGRAM
2.1 General Obligations
Vendor shall establish, implement, and maintain a comprehensive written information-security program (the "Security Program") that includes administrative, technical, and physical safeguards designed to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of Customer Data. The Security Program shall be reasonably designed to:
(a) identify and assess internal and external risks to the security, confidentiality, integrity, and availability of Customer Data;
(b) implement and maintain safeguards to control the risks identified through such assessment, including the specific controls described in this Exhibit;
(c) regularly test and monitor the effectiveness of such safeguards; and
(d) evaluate and adjust the Security Program in light of changes to Vendor's business operations, threat landscape, or the results of testing and monitoring activities.
The Security Program shall be consistent with industry-standard frameworks, including, without limitation, the requirements set forth in ISO/IEC 27001:2022 (Information Security, Cybersecurity and Privacy Protection — Information Security Management Systems — Requirements) and the Trust Services Criteria promulgated by the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA) for SOC 2 examinations, as each may be updated from time to time.
Vendor shall designate a qualified security officer (e.g., Chief Information Security Officer or equivalent) who shall be responsible for the oversight, implementation, and enforcement of the Security Program. Vendor shall provide the name and contact information of such security officer to Customer upon reasonable written request.
2.2 Risk Assessments
Vendor shall conduct comprehensive internal risk assessments of its information-security environment no less frequently than once per calendar year. Such risk assessments shall evaluate threats and vulnerabilities applicable to the systems, networks, and processes involved in the storage, processing, and transmission of Customer Data.
Upon completion of each risk assessment, Vendor shall categorize identified findings according to severity (e.g., critical, high, medium, low) and shall remediate or mitigate identified high-severity and critical-severity findings within timeframes commensurate with the severity of each finding. As a general guideline, critical-severity findings shall be remediated or mitigated within thirty (30) calendar days, and high-severity findings shall be remediated or mitigated within sixty (60) calendar days, unless circumstances beyond Vendor's reasonable control necessitate a longer remediation period, in which case Vendor shall implement interim compensating controls.
Vendor shall maintain documentation of risk-assessment results, remediation activities, and the status of outstanding findings for a minimum period of three (3) years; provided, however, that nothing in this Section 2.2 obligates Vendor to disclose such documentation to Customer except to the extent required under Section 5 (SOC 2 Reporting) or Section 7 (Security-Incident Notification and Response) of this Exhibit.
3. ENCRYPTION STANDARDS
3.1 Data at Rest
All Customer Data at rest—including, without limitation, data stored in databases, file systems, object storage, backup media, and any other persistent storage mechanisms—shall be encrypted using the Advanced Encryption Standard with a minimum key length of two hundred fifty-six (256) bits (AES-256), or an equivalent or stronger encryption algorithm generally recognized as providing comparable or superior protection by the cryptographic community at the time of implementation.
Encryption keys used for the encryption of Customer Data at rest shall be managed in accordance with Vendor's key-management policy, which shall include, at a minimum, procedures for the secure generation, storage, distribution, rotation, and destruction of encryption keys. Encryption keys shall be rotated no less frequently than once per calendar year, and Vendor shall maintain the ability to decrypt data encrypted under prior keys for the duration of any applicable retention period.
3.2 Data in Transit
All Customer Data in transit—including data transmitted between Customer environments and the Platform, between components of the Platform (including inter-service and inter-data-center communications), and between the Platform and any third-party system or subcontractor—shall be encrypted using Transport Layer Security version 1.3 (TLS 1.3) or a later version of the TLS protocol offering equivalent or superior protection.
Vendor shall disable all deprecated, insecure, or otherwise obsolete cipher suites and protocol versions across all endpoints, application programming interfaces (APIs), and network interfaces that handle Customer Data. Without limiting the foregoing, Vendor shall ensure that SSLv2, SSLv3, TLS 1.0, and TLS 1.1 are disabled on all such systems, and that only cipher suites supporting forward secrecy are enabled.
3.3 Key Management
Encryption keys shall be stored separately from the encrypted data they protect. Under no circumstances shall encryption keys be stored in the same database, file system, or storage volume as the Customer Data encrypted using such keys.
Vendor shall use hardware security modules (HSMs) or equivalent key-storage mechanisms that have been validated to Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) 140-2 Level 2 or higher (or the successor FIPS 140-3 standard at an equivalent or higher security level) for the generation, storage, and management of production encryption keys. Where cloud-based key-management services are utilized, such services must meet or exceed the FIPS 140-2 Level 2 validation requirement.
4. ACCESS CONTROL
4.1 Logical Access Controls
Vendor shall enforce role-based access control (RBAC) across all systems, applications, and infrastructure components that store, process, or transmit Customer Data. Access rights shall be granted on a least-privilege, need-to-know basis, ensuring that each individual user is granted only the minimum permissions necessary to perform that user's assigned job responsibilities.
Multi-factor authentication (MFA) shall be required for all Vendor personnel and subcontractor personnel accessing systems that store or process Customer Data. MFA shall consist of at least two of the following factors: (i) something the user knows (e.g., password or passphrase), (ii) something the user has (e.g., hardware token, mobile authenticator application, or smart card), or (iii) something the user is (e.g., biometric identifier). For the avoidance of doubt, SMS-based one-time passcodes shall not be considered an acceptable MFA factor for privileged administrative access.
All user accounts on production systems shall be assigned unique user identifiers. Shared, generic, or group accounts shall not be used on production systems that store or process Customer Data. Where service accounts are necessary for automated processes, such accounts shall be individually identified, restricted to the minimum required privileges, and subject to regular review.
4.2 Access Reviews
Vendor shall conduct access-entitlement reviews no less frequently than once per calendar quarter. During each quarterly review, Vendor shall verify that all active access rights to systems storing or processing Customer Data remain appropriate for each user's current role and responsibilities. Any access rights identified as excessive, unnecessary, or otherwise inappropriate during such review shall be promptly revoked or adjusted.
Access for any individual whose role no longer requires access to Customer Data—including, without limitation, personnel who have been reassigned, transferred, or whose employment or engagement with Vendor or a subcontractor has been terminated—shall be deprovisioned within twenty-four (24) hours of the effective date of the personnel change or separation. In the case of involuntary terminations for cause, access shall be revoked immediately upon notice of the termination event.
4.3 Physical Access Controls
Data-center facilities housing Customer Data—whether owned, operated, leased, or contracted by Vendor or its subcontractors—shall maintain physical access controls designed to prevent unauthorized physical access to, or tampering with, systems and infrastructure. Such physical access controls shall include, at a minimum:
(a) badge-access or biometric-access entry systems at all facility entry points, with access limited to authorized personnel;
(b) visitor management procedures, including sign-in and sign-out logs, escort requirements for non-authorized visitors, and issuance of temporary, visually distinct visitor badges;
(c) twenty-four hours per day, seven days per week (24/7) video surveillance of facility entry and exit points, server rooms, and other sensitive areas, with surveillance recordings retained for a minimum of ninety (90) calendar days; and
(d) environmental controls, including fire suppression, climate control, and water-leak detection systems, designed to protect infrastructure from environmental hazards.
5. SOC 2 REPORTING
5.1 Audit Firm and Report Type
Vendor shall engage Deloitte & Touche LLP (or a successor nationally recognized independent audit firm reasonably selected by Vendor and approved in writing by Vendor; provided that Vendor shall not be required to obtain Customer's consent to the selection of an audit firm, so long as such firm is a "Big Four" accounting firm or a nationally recognized firm of equivalent stature) to perform an annual SOC 2 Type I examination covering the Trust Services Criteria for Security, Availability, and Confidentiality applicable to the Platform and the services provided thereunder.
The SOC 2 Type I report shall evaluate the suitability of the design of Vendor's controls as of a specified point in time (the "Examination Date"). The Examination Date for each annual report shall fall within the twelve (12) month period preceding the delivery of such report to Customer. Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to align the Examination Date with the end of Vendor's fiscal year or such other date as Vendor may determine in its reasonable discretion.
For the avoidance of doubt, nothing in this Section 5 obligates Vendor to obtain a SOC 2 Type II report (which evaluates operating effectiveness over a period of time) unless the parties separately agree to such an obligation in writing.
5.2 Delivery of Reports
Vendor shall deliver a complete copy of each SOC 2 Type I report to Customer within thirty (30) calendar days following Vendor's receipt of the final report from Deloitte & Touche LLP (or the applicable successor audit firm). Delivery shall be made electronically to Customer's designated security contact or through a secure document-sharing mechanism designated by Vendor.
All SOC 2 reports delivered to Customer pursuant to this Section 5.2 shall be provided under, and subject to, the confidentiality obligations set forth in the Agreement. Customer shall not disclose, distribute, or make available any SOC 2 report (or any portion thereof) to any third party without Vendor's prior written consent, except to the extent required by applicable law, regulation, or legal process, or to Customer's external auditors or regulators who are bound by obligations of confidentiality no less restrictive than those set forth in the Agreement.
5.3 Complementary User-Entity Controls
Each SOC 2 report delivered pursuant to this Exhibit shall identify any complementary user-entity controls ("CUECs") that Customer is expected to implement within its own environment in order for Vendor's controls to operate as designed. Customer acknowledges and agrees that it is solely responsible for implementing all applicable CUECs within its own environment. Vendor shall not be responsible for any control deficiency, data loss, or security event arising from Customer's failure to implement applicable CUECs.
Upon Customer's reasonable written request, Vendor shall provide clarification or additional guidance regarding the implementation of identified CUECs; provided that such assistance shall not obligate Vendor to perform consulting services or implement controls within Customer's environment.
5.4 Remediation of Exceptions
In the event that a SOC 2 Type I report identifies one or more control-design exceptions (i.e., instances in which the design of a specified control does not meet the applicable Trust Services Criteria), Vendor shall:
(a) develop a written remediation plan describing the specific corrective actions Vendor intends to implement to address each identified exception, including responsible parties, milestones, and target completion dates;
(b) deliver such remediation plan to Customer within thirty (30) calendar days of the date of the SOC 2 report in which the exception is identified; and
(c) use commercially reasonable efforts to implement the remediation plan and resolve all identified exceptions within ninety (90) calendar days following delivery of the remediation plan to Customer.
If Vendor determines that remediation of any exception will require more than ninety (90) calendar days, Vendor shall notify Customer in writing of the anticipated timeline and the interim compensating controls that Vendor has implemented or plans to implement to mitigate the risk associated with the identified exception during the remediation period.
6. NETWORK AND INFRASTRUCTURE SECURITY
6.1 Firewalls and Intrusion Detection
Vendor shall deploy and maintain next-generation firewalls (NGFWs), intrusion-detection systems (IDS), and intrusion-prevention systems (IPS) at all network perimeters and at critical internal network segments within the Platform environment. Firewall rules and network segmentation policies shall be reviewed and updated no less frequently than semi-annually, and shall be configured to deny all traffic by default except that which is explicitly authorized by documented policy.
Vendor shall maintain the capability to detect, log, and respond to malicious network activity, including but not limited to distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks, unauthorized port scanning, and lateral movement attempts within the Platform environment.
6.2 Vulnerability Management
Vendor shall implement and maintain a vulnerability-management program that includes automated vulnerability scanning of all production infrastructure, including servers, network devices, containers, and cloud resources, no less frequently than once per calendar month. Ad hoc scans shall be performed following any material change to the production environment.
Identified vulnerabilities shall be prioritized and remediated or mitigated in accordance with the following timelines, measured from the date of identification:

Where remediation within the applicable timeline is not feasible due to operational constraints (e.g., vendor patch unavailability, risk of production disruption), Vendor shall implement interim compensating controls sufficient to mitigate the identified risk and shall document the rationale for any extension.
6.3 Patch Management
Vendor shall maintain a patch-management program designed to ensure that security patches and updates are applied to production systems in a timely manner. Security patches classified as critical—whether by the applicable third-party software vendor, by Vendor's internal vulnerability-management team, or by reference to the applicable CVSS score—shall be applied to production systems within fourteen (14) calendar days of general availability of the patch. All other security patches shall be applied within thirty (30) calendar days of general availability.
Emergency patches addressing actively exploited zero-day vulnerabilities shall be applied on an expedited basis, with a target timeline of seventy-two (72) hours from the date the patch is made generally available. Vendor shall maintain a patch-testing process to minimize the risk of production disruption resulting from patch deployment.
7. SECURITY-INCIDENT NOTIFICATION AND RESPONSE
7.1 Definitions.  For purposes of this Exhibit, "Security Incident" means any confirmed unauthorized access to, acquisition of, use of, or disclosure of Customer Data, or any event that materially compromises the security, confidentiality, or integrity of the Platform or Customer Data. For the avoidance of doubt, the term "Security Incident" does not include (a) unsuccessful login attempts, port scans, or other routine network probes that do not result in unauthorized access; (b) automated vulnerability scans or penetration tests conducted by or on behalf of Vendor in the ordinary course; or (c) denial-of-service attacks that do not result in unauthorized access to Customer Data, unless such attacks materially impact the availability of the Platform for a period exceeding the recovery-time objective set forth in Section 11.
7.2 Notification Timeline
Vendor shall notify Customer of any Security Incident within seventy-two (72) hours of Vendor's becoming aware of such Security Incident. For purposes of this Section 7.2, Vendor shall be deemed "aware" of a Security Incident at the time at which a member of Vendor's security or incident-response team has confirmed that a Security Incident has occurred (as distinguished from a preliminary investigation of a potential security event).
Notification shall be provided to Customer's designated security contact via both email and telephone, with written confirmation to follow within twenty-four (24) hours of the initial notification. Customer shall maintain current designated security-contact information on file with Vendor and shall promptly notify Vendor of any changes to such information.
7.3 Content of Notification
The initial notification provided under Section 7.2 shall include the following information, to the extent known at the time of notification:
(a) the date and time the Security Incident was discovered by Vendor;
(b) a description of the nature and scope of the Security Incident, including the categories and approximate number of Customer Data records affected (or, if such information is not yet known, a good-faith estimate);
(c) a description of the corrective actions taken or planned by Vendor to contain, investigate, and remediate the Security Incident;
(d) the identity and contact information of Vendor's incident-response lead or other designated point of contact for communications regarding the Security Incident; and
(e) any recommendations for actions that Customer should take to mitigate potential harm resulting from the Security Incident.
Vendor acknowledges that the initial notification may be based on preliminary information and that the facts surrounding the Security Incident may evolve as the investigation progresses. Nothing in this Section 7.3 shall be construed to require Vendor to delay notification in order to compile a complete initial notification.
7.4 Ongoing Communication
During the active investigation and remediation of a Security Incident, Vendor shall provide written status updates to Customer at least every forty-eight (48) hours. Such updates shall include, at a minimum, a summary of investigative findings since the last update, a description of any additional corrective actions taken, and an estimated timeline for resolution. The forty-eight (48) hour update cycle shall continue until Vendor reasonably determines that the Security Incident has been contained and remediated, at which time Vendor shall notify Customer that the Security Incident has been resolved.
7.5 Root-Cause Analysis
Within thirty (30) calendar days following the containment of a Security Incident, Vendor shall deliver to Customer a written root-cause analysis report. Such report shall include, at a minimum:
(a) a detailed description of the Security Incident, including the root cause(s) identified;
(b) a timeline of key events, from initial compromise (if applicable) through detection, containment, and remediation;
(c) a description of the data and systems affected;
(d) an assessment of the impact of the Security Incident on Customer Data;
(e) a remediation plan describing the specific actions Vendor will take (or has already taken) to prevent recurrence of similar incidents, together with a timeline for implementation of such actions; and
(f) any lessons learned and process improvements identified as a result of the investigation.
7.6 Cooperation.  Vendor shall reasonably cooperate with Customer's own investigation and any regulatory-notification obligations arising from a Security Incident, including but not limited to:
(a) preservation of forensic evidence and logs related to the Security Incident for a minimum of one (1) year following containment, or such longer period as may be required by applicable law;
(b) making Vendor's incident-response personnel reasonably available for interviews, meetings, or calls with Customer's security, legal, or compliance teams;
(c) providing reasonable assistance in the preparation of any notifications required to be sent by Customer to affected individuals, regulators, or other third parties; and
(d) coordinating with Customer on public communications related to the Security Incident, to the extent such communications reference Customer or Customer Data.
Customer and Vendor shall each bear their own costs in connection with their respective investigation and response activities, except as otherwise provided in the Agreement.
8. DATA-HANDLING PROCEDURES
8.1 Data Segregation
Customer Data shall be logically segregated from the data of Vendor's other customers at the application and database layers. Such logical segregation shall be designed to prevent unauthorized access to, or commingling of, Customer Data with the data of any other Vendor customer. Vendor shall implement and maintain controls to validate the effectiveness of such logical segregation on an ongoing basis.
8.2 Data Classification
Vendor shall treat all Customer Data as "Confidential" (or the equivalent highest-sensitivity classification under Vendor's data-classification policy, if Vendor does not use the term "Confidential") unless a higher classification is specified by Customer in writing. Upon written request from Customer, Vendor shall apply an elevated classification (e.g., "Highly Confidential" or "Restricted") to designated categories of Customer Data, and Vendor shall apply the additional handling controls specified by Vendor's data-classification policy for such elevated classification.
8.3 Backup and Recovery
Vendor shall perform encrypted backups of Customer Data no less frequently than once per calendar day. All backup media and backup data shall be encrypted using standards no less protective than those set forth in Section 3.1 of this Exhibit.
Backups shall be stored in a geographically separate facility from the primary production environment. For purposes of this Section 8.3, "geographically separate" means a facility located in a different geographic region or availability zone, as applicable, such that a single localized event (e.g., natural disaster, power outage) affecting the primary production facility would not simultaneously affect the backup facility.
Vendor shall test backup-restoration procedures no less frequently than semi-annually (i.e., at least twice per calendar year) to verify the integrity, completeness, and recoverability of backup data. Vendor shall maintain documentation of the results of each backup-restoration test.
8.4 Data Destruction
Upon termination or expiration of the Agreement, and subject to Section 20 of the Agreement (regarding data-return and transition obligations), Vendor shall securely delete or destroy all Customer Data in Vendor's possession or control—including all copies, replicas, backups, and archived instances of Customer Data—within ninety (90) calendar days following the effective date of termination or expiration. Deletion or destruction shall be performed using methods consistent with the National Institute of Standards and Technology Special Publication 800-88 Revision 1 (Guidelines for Media Sanitization), or a successor publication providing equivalent or more rigorous standards.
Upon Customer's written request, Vendor shall provide written certification of the destruction of Customer Data, signed by an authorized representative of Vendor, within thirty (30) calendar days of the completion of the destruction process. Such certification shall confirm the date of destruction, the method(s) used, and the categories of data destroyed.
Notwithstanding the foregoing, Vendor may retain Customer Data to the extent required by applicable law, regulation, or legal hold obligation, provided that (a) Vendor notifies Customer of such retention requirement to the extent permitted by law, (b) such retained data continues to be subject to the confidentiality and security obligations of the Agreement and this Exhibit, and (c) Vendor shall destroy such retained data promptly upon the expiration of the applicable retention obligation.
9. LOGGING AND MONITORING
9.1 Audit Logs
Vendor shall maintain comprehensive audit logs for all access to and modifications of Customer Data. Each audit-log entry shall include, at a minimum, the following information:
(a) the unique user identifier of the individual or service account performing the action;
(b) the date and time of the action (recorded in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC));
(c) a description of the action performed (e.g., read, create, update, delete, export);
(d) the resource(s) or data element(s) affected by the action; and
(e) the source IP address or other identifying information of the system from which the action was initiated.
Audit logs shall be retained for a minimum of twelve (12) months in an online, searchable format. Following the twelve-month online retention period, audit logs shall be retained in archived (offline) storage for an additional twelve (12) months, for a total minimum retention period of twenty-four (24) months. Audit logs shall be protected against unauthorized modification or deletion through the use of write-once storage, cryptographic integrity controls, or equivalent tamper-evident mechanisms.
9.2 Monitoring.  Vendor shall implement twenty-four hours per day, seven days per week (24/7) real-time monitoring and alerting on security events across the Platform environment. Such monitoring shall include, without limitation, automated detection and alerting for anomalous login behavior, privilege escalation events, unauthorized configuration changes, data-exfiltration indicators, and other events consistent with industry-standard threat-detection frameworks (e.g., the MITRE ATT&CK framework).
Vendor shall maintain a security operations center (SOC) or equivalent capability staffed by trained security personnel responsible for triaging, investigating, and responding to security alerts on a continuous basis.
10. PERSONNEL SECURITY
Vendor shall conduct background checks on all personnel—including employees, contractors, and subcontractor personnel—who will have access to Customer Data prior to granting such access, to the extent permitted by applicable law and regulation. Background checks shall include, at a minimum, verification of identity, criminal-history checks, and employment-history verification, as applicable and as permitted by the jurisdiction in which such personnel are located.
All Vendor personnel with access to Customer Data shall complete information-security awareness training upon hire or initial engagement and at least annually thereafter. Such training shall cover, at a minimum, topics related to phishing and social-engineering awareness, password hygiene, data-handling best practices, acceptable use of Vendor systems, and incident-reporting procedures.
Vendor shall ensure that all personnel with access to Customer Data are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than those set forth in the Agreement. Upon Customer's reasonable written request, Vendor shall confirm that such confidentiality obligations are in place.
11. BUSINESS CONTINUITY AND DISASTER RECOVERY
Vendor shall maintain a documented business-continuity and disaster-recovery plan (the "BC/DR Plan") for the Platform, designed to minimize the impact of disruptive events on the availability and integrity of Customer Data and the Platform. The BC/DR Plan shall address, at a minimum, the following scenarios: natural disaster, power failure, network outage, hardware failure, cyberattack, and pandemic or other workforce-disruption event.
Vendor shall test the BC/DR Plan no less frequently than once per calendar year. Testing shall include, at a minimum, tabletop exercises and functional failover tests designed to validate the effectiveness of recovery procedures and the achievability of the recovery objectives set forth below.
Vendor shall maintain the following recovery objectives for the Platform:
Recovery-Point Objective (RPO): four (4) hours, meaning that in the event of a disaster or disruptive event, the maximum period of data loss shall not exceed four (4) hours of transactions or data changes.
Recovery-Time Objective (RTO): eight (8) hours, meaning that in the event of a disaster or disruptive event, the Platform shall be restored to operational status within eight (8) hours of the declaration of a disaster event.
Vendor shall notify Customer of any activation of its disaster-recovery plan within four (4) hours of such activation. Such notification shall include the nature of the disruptive event, the anticipated impact on the Platform and Customer Data, and the estimated timeline for recovery. Vendor shall provide ongoing status updates to Customer at reasonable intervals until the Platform has been restored to normal operational status.
12. MODIFICATIONS TO SECURITY STANDARDS
Vendor reserves the right to modify, update, or enhance its Security Program and the security standards set forth in this Exhibit from time to time in its reasonable discretion to address changes in the threat landscape, regulatory requirements, industry best practices, or Vendor's operational environment; provided, however, that no such modification shall materially reduce the level of protection afforded to Customer Data below the standards set forth in this Exhibit during the Term.
Vendor shall notify Customer in writing of any material modification to the security standards set forth in this Exhibit at least thirty (30) calendar days prior to the implementation of such modification. For purposes of this Section 12, a "material modification" means any change that would (a) reduce the encryption standards applicable to Customer Data below those specified in Section 3, (b) materially weaken access controls, (c) extend remediation timelines for vulnerabilities or Security Incidents beyond those specified herein, or (d) otherwise materially diminish the protections afforded to Customer Data under this Exhibit.
If Customer reasonably determines that a proposed material modification would adversely affect the security of Customer Data, Customer may object to such modification by providing written notice to Vendor within fifteen (15) calendar days of receipt of Vendor's modification notice. The parties shall thereafter negotiate in good faith to resolve Customer's objection. If the parties are unable to reach agreement within thirty (30) calendar days of Customer's objection, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form(s) in accordance with the termination provisions of the Agreement.
13. GENERAL PROVISIONS
Limitation of Liability. This Exhibit is subject to, and the obligations of the parties hereunder shall be governed by, the limitation-of-liability provisions set forth in Section 16 of the Agreement. Nothing in this Exhibit shall be construed to create any liability obligation that is broader than, or in addition to, the liability framework established by the Agreement.
Sole Remedy. Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for Vendor's failure to meet the security standards, reporting obligations, or data-handling procedures set forth in this Exhibit shall be as set forth in the Agreement, including, without limitation, any applicable service-level credits, indemnification obligations, or termination rights specified therein.
Survival. The following provisions of this Exhibit shall survive the termination or expiration of the Agreement for any reason: Section 7 (Security-Incident Notification and Response), Section 8.4 (Data Destruction), and Section 9.1 (Audit Logs), with respect to the retention periods specified therein. Such survival shall be in addition to, and shall not limit, any survival provisions set forth in the body of the Agreement.
No Third-Party Beneficiaries. Nothing in this Exhibit is intended to, or shall be construed to, confer any rights or benefits upon any person or entity other than the parties to the Agreement and their respective permitted successors and assigns.

EXHIBIT D
ACCEPTABLE USE POLICY
to the Trey Research Vendor Agreement v.4.2
Doc ID: TR-EA-2026-0417
This Acceptable Use Policy ("AUP") is incorporated by reference into the Trey Research Vendor Agreement v.4.2 (the "Agreement") by and between Trey Research, a Delaware corporation ("Vendor"), and the customer identified in the Agreement ("Customer"). Capitalized terms not defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the Agreement. This AUP governs Customer's access to and use of the Trey Research AI platform and all related services, APIs, models, and outputs provided thereunder (collectively, the "Platform"). Customer's use of the Platform at any time during the Term is expressly conditioned upon Customer's ongoing compliance with the terms and conditions of this AUP, as the same may be modified from time to time in accordance with Section 7 hereof.
1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
1.1 This AUP establishes the rules, restrictions, and conditions under which Customer and its Authorized Users may access and use the Trey Research AI platform (the "Platform"), including all artificial intelligence models, machine learning models, application programming interfaces ("APIs"), dashboards, user interfaces, outputs, generated content, inference results, analytical reports, documentation, and any other materials or functionality made available by Vendor to Customer pursuant to the Agreement. The purpose of this AUP is to protect the integrity, security, performance, and availability of the Platform, to safeguard the rights and interests of Vendor and its other customers, and to ensure that Customer's use of the Platform complies with applicable law and the terms of the Agreement.
1.2 All use of the Platform by Customer, its employees, officers, directors, agents, contractors, consultants, and Authorized Users (as that term is defined in the Agreement) is subject to this AUP at all times during the Term. Customer acknowledges and agrees that compliance with this AUP is a material obligation under the Agreement and that any breach of this AUP shall constitute a breach of the Agreement. Customer is responsible for ensuring that each individual or entity that accesses or uses the Platform through Customer's accounts, credentials, or systems is made aware of the requirements of this AUP and complies with its terms in full.
1.3 This AUP constitutes the sole policy governing acceptable use of the Platform under the Agreement. No additional schedules, appendices, annexes, or subcontractor lists are appended to or incorporated within this Exhibit D. To the extent that any other document referenced in or delivered under the Agreement addresses matters related to acceptable use, such document shall be deemed supplementary to, and shall not supersede or limit, the requirements of this AUP unless the Agreement expressly provides otherwise.
2. PERMITTED USES
2.1 Internal Business Operations. Customer may use the Platform solely for Customer's internal business operations as described in the applicable Statement of Work executed under the Agreement, including, without limitation, the processing of underwriting decisions, risk scoring, claims triage, policy pricing analytics, portfolio risk assessment, and related analytics within the scope of the license granted under the Agreement. Customer shall not use the Platform for any purpose outside the scope of the use case or use cases specified in the applicable Statement of Work without Vendor's prior written consent.
2.2 Authorized User Access. Customer may permit access to the Platform by its Authorized Users, provided that Customer remains fully responsible for ensuring that all Authorized Users comply with this AUP and with the terms and conditions of the Agreement. Customer shall ensure that each Authorized User accesses the Platform only through the authentication mechanisms and credential management procedures specified by Vendor. Customer shall not permit any individual or entity to access the Platform using the credentials of another Authorized User and shall promptly revoke access for any Authorized User who is no longer authorized to use the Platform on Customer's behalf, including upon such individual's termination of employment or engagement with Customer.
2.3 Integration with Internal Systems. Customer may integrate Platform outputs, including model inference results, risk scores, decision recommendations, and analytical reports, into its internal systems, workflows, decision pipelines, and reporting frameworks in accordance with the technical specifications, integration guidelines, and data-handling requirements set forth in the Agreement and its Exhibits. Any such integration shall be performed in a manner consistent with the security requirements and data-handling obligations set forth in the Agreement and applicable law.
2.4 Documentation and Training. Customer may use Vendor-provided documentation, technical guides, and training materials solely for the purpose of enabling Customer's Authorized Users to access and use the Platform in compliance with the Agreement and this AUP.
3. PROHIBITED USES
Customer shall not, and shall not permit any Authorized User or third party to, engage in any of the following activities in connection with the Platform. The prohibitions set forth in this Section 3 apply to all components of the Platform, including all models, APIs, outputs, data, documentation, and infrastructure made available by Vendor.
3.1 Reverse Engineering and Decompilation
(a) Customer shall not reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble, or otherwise attempt to derive the source code, algorithms, model architectures, model weights, neural network topologies, training methodologies, optimization techniques, feature engineering processes, or any other proprietary components of the Platform or any AI models, machine learning models, or analytical engines accessible through the Platform. This prohibition applies regardless of the method employed, including but not limited to static analysis, dynamic analysis, binary inspection, bytecode decompilation, or any other technique.
(b) Customer shall not attempt to extract, reconstruct, replicate, or approximate model parameters, hyperparameters, embedding vectors, attention mechanisms, loss functions, or training data through probing, adversarial querying, model inversion, membership inference, prompt injection, side-channel analysis, gradient estimation, distillation techniques, or any analogous technique. This prohibition applies to all models and model versions deployed within the Platform, whether proprietary to Vendor or licensed by Vendor from third-party model providers.
(c) For the avoidance of doubt, the restrictions set forth in this Section 3.1 are in addition to, and do not limit, any intellectual property protections, trade secret protections, or confidentiality obligations set forth in the Agreement.
3.2 Competitive Benchmarking
(a) Customer shall not use the Platform, or any outputs, performance data, latency metrics, throughput statistics, accuracy scores, precision and recall metrics, inference times, error rates, or other results derived from the Platform, for the purpose of competitive benchmarking, competitive analysis, comparative evaluation, or market intelligence gathering against any competing product, service, platform, or technology, whether offered by Customer, an affiliate of Customer, or any third party.
(b) Customer shall not publish, disclose, distribute, or share with any third party any performance-related data, benchmarking results, evaluation metrics, test outcomes, or comparative analyses pertaining to the Platform without Vendor's prior written consent. This restriction applies to disclosures in any medium, including academic publications, industry reports, conference presentations, blog posts, social media, press releases, and analyst briefings.
(c) Nothing in this Section 3.2 shall restrict Customer from disclosing performance data to Vendor for the purpose of reporting issues, requesting technical support, or participating in Vendor-sponsored product feedback programs, provided that such disclosures are made directly to Vendor and in accordance with the confidentiality provisions of the Agreement.
3.3 Unlawful or Harmful Purposes
(a) Customer shall not use the Platform for any purpose that violates applicable federal, state, local, or international law, regulation, ordinance, rule, or binding governmental guidance, including but not limited to laws and regulations governing insurance underwriting, insurance pricing, insurance claims handling, consumer protection, unfair and deceptive trade practices, anti-discrimination (including disparate impact and disparate treatment), fair lending, fair housing, data privacy and data protection (including the California Consumer Privacy Act, the EU General Data Protection Regulation, and analogous state, national, and international data protection laws), export control, economic sanctions, anti-money laundering, and anti-bribery and anti-corruption.
(b) Customer shall not use the Platform to process data or generate outputs that facilitate, enable, or contribute to fraud, identity theft, impersonation, harassment, stalking, defamation, libel, slander, extortion, or any form of unlawful discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.
(c) Customer shall not input into the Platform any data that Customer does not have the legal right to process, including, without limitation, data collected without requisite consent or authorization, data subject to a legal hold or litigation preservation obligation that prohibits processing, data obtained through unlawful means, or data the processing of which would violate any applicable privacy policy, terms of service, or contractual obligation to which Customer is bound.
(d) Customer shall not use the Platform to generate, store, process, or transmit content that constitutes or promotes child sexual abuse material, terrorism, violent extremism, or the manufacture of weapons, explosives, or controlled substances.
3.4 Unauthorized Access and Security Violations
(a) Customer shall not attempt to gain unauthorized access to any portion of the Platform, Vendor's systems, networks, servers, databases, or infrastructure, or to any accounts, data, configurations, or resources belonging to other Vendor customers, Vendor's partners, or any third party. This prohibition includes any attempt to escalate privileges, bypass multi-factor authentication, exploit software vulnerabilities, or access administrative or management interfaces not designated for Customer's use.
(b) Customer shall not introduce viruses, malware, worms, Trojan horses, ransomware, spyware, adware, rootkits, keyloggers, or other malicious code, scripts, or programs into the Platform or any system or network connected to the Platform.
(c) Customer shall not conduct penetration testing, vulnerability scanning, red-team exercises, security audits, stress testing, or load testing against the Platform, Vendor's APIs, or any associated infrastructure without Vendor's prior written authorization. Any such authorized testing must be conducted in strict accordance with the scope, schedule, and methodology approved by Vendor in writing.
(d) Customer shall not circumvent, disable, impair, or interfere with any security features, authentication mechanisms, encryption protocols, access-control lists, digital rights management protections, or other protective measures implemented by Vendor in connection with the Platform.
(e) Customer shall not intercept, monitor, capture, or record network traffic, API calls, or data transmissions between the Platform and any other system, except to the extent expressly required for Customer's authorized integration activities and performed in compliance with applicable law.
3.5 Excessive or Abusive Usage
(a) Customer shall not use the Platform in a manner that exceeds the usage parameters set forth in the Agreement or the applicable Statement of Work, including, without limitation, exceeding the Monthly Decision Volume Threshold, applicable API rate limits, concurrent session limits, data storage quotas, or bandwidth allocations, except as expressly permitted under the Agreement's overage provisions. Customer acknowledges that usage in excess of applicable thresholds may result in the imposition of overage fees, throttling, or suspension of access, as described in the Agreement.
(b) Customer shall not engage in automated, scripted, bot-driven, or programmatic usage patterns designed to circumvent, evade, or manipulate usage metering, rate limiting, throttling mechanisms, concurrency controls, or billing mechanisms. Customer shall not employ techniques designed to fragment, distribute, or restructure API calls for the purpose of avoiding usage thresholds or triggering lower-tier pricing.
(c) Customer shall not use the Platform in a manner that generates unnecessary or excessive data requests, redundant processing cycles, or otherwise wasteful consumption of Platform resources, where such use serves no legitimate business purpose within the scope of the applicable Statement of Work.
3.6 Resale and Unauthorized Distribution
(a) Customer shall not resell, sublicense, redistribute, rent, lease, lend, transfer, assign, or otherwise make available the Platform, any component of the Platform, or any access credentials or tokens for the Platform to any third party, except as expressly authorized in writing in the Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, this prohibition includes providing access to affiliates of Customer that are not named as authorized entities in the Agreement.
(b) Customer shall not use the Platform to provide a competing managed service, bureau service, outsourced processing service, analytics-as-a-service offering, or any other commercial service to third parties in which the Platform or its outputs form a material component of the service delivered to such third parties. This prohibition applies regardless of whether Customer charges fees to such third parties for the service.
(c) Customer shall not frame, mirror, scrape, or otherwise replicate any portion of the Platform's user interface, dashboards, or output displays for distribution to third parties.
3.7 Interference with Platform Operations
(a) Customer shall not take any action that imposes an unreasonable or disproportionate load on Vendor's infrastructure, servers, networks, storage systems, or processing resources, or that degrades, disrupts, or threatens to degrade Platform performance, availability, or reliability for other Vendor customers or for Vendor's own operations.
(b) Customer shall not interfere with, disrupt, or attempt to disrupt the integrity, availability, security, or performance of the Platform, including by initiating or participating in denial-of-service attacks, distributed denial-of-service attacks, resource exhaustion attacks, or any similar activity.
(c) Customer shall not modify, alter, tamper with, or destroy any data, logs, audit trails, or metadata maintained by Vendor in connection with Customer's use of the Platform.
4. CUSTOMER RESPONSIBILITIES
4.1 Authorized User Compliance. Customer is solely responsible for ensuring that all Authorized Users are made aware of and comply with this AUP prior to and throughout the duration of their access to the Platform. Customer shall provide each Authorized User with a copy of this AUP or with a summary of its material terms and conditions sufficient to enable such Authorized User to understand and comply with all applicable restrictions. Customer shall maintain records of such distribution and awareness activities and shall make such records available to Vendor upon reasonable request.
4.2 Administrative, Technical, and Organizational Measures. Customer shall implement and maintain reasonable administrative, technical, and organizational measures to prevent unauthorized use of the Platform and to ensure compliance with this AUP. Such measures shall include, at a minimum, the following:
(a) implementation of access controls, including role-based access permissions, unique user credentials, and multi-factor authentication where supported by the Platform;
(b) periodic review of Authorized User access privileges and prompt deprovisioning of accounts for individuals who no longer require access;
(c) maintenance of audit logs and access records sufficient to support investigation of suspected AUP violations; and
(d) implementation of policies and procedures governing the acceptable use of AI-generated outputs within Customer's internal decision-making processes, consistent with applicable law and regulatory guidance.
4.3 Notification of Violations. Customer shall promptly notify Vendor in writing upon becoming aware of any actual or suspected violation of this AUP by any Authorized User, employee, contractor, agent, or third party accessing the Platform through Customer's accounts, credentials, API keys, or systems. Such notice shall include a description of the suspected violation, the identity of the individual or entity involved (to the extent known), and the remedial actions Customer has taken or intends to take. Customer shall cooperate with Vendor in investigating and remediating any such violation.
4.4 Responsibility for Third-Party Access. To the extent Customer provides access to the Platform to any subcontractor, agent, or other third party in accordance with the Agreement, Customer shall ensure that such subcontractor, agent, or third party is bound by obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in this AUP and shall remain fully liable for any breach of this AUP by such subcontractor, agent, or third party.
5. MONITORING AND ENFORCEMENT
5.1 Vendor's Monitoring Rights. Vendor reserves the right, but shall not be obligated, to monitor Customer's use of the Platform for compliance with this AUP, the Agreement, and applicable law. Such monitoring may include, without limitation, the use of automated tools, usage analytics engines, anomaly detection systems, log review and analysis, API call pattern analysis, and any other monitoring mechanisms that Vendor deems appropriate in its sole discretion.
5.2 No Obligation to Monitor. Vendor is not obligated to monitor Customer's use of the Platform and shall not be liable for any failure to detect or prevent any violation of this AUP by Customer or its Authorized Users. The fact that Vendor may or may not engage in monitoring at any given time shall not affect Customer's obligations under this AUP or the Agreement.
5.3 Cooperation with Investigations. In the event that Vendor initiates an investigation into a suspected violation of this AUP, Customer shall cooperate fully with such investigation, including by providing access to relevant logs, records, data, personnel, and systems as reasonably requested by Vendor. Customer's failure to cooperate with any such investigation shall itself constitute a violation of this AUP.
6. SUSPENSION OF SERVICE FOR AUP VIOLATIONS
6.1 Vendor's Right to Suspend. Vendor reserves the right, in its sole and absolute discretion, to immediately suspend Customer's access to the Platform, in whole or in part, upon Vendor's determination that Customer or any Authorized User has violated or is violating this AUP, or upon Vendor's reasonable belief that such a violation is imminent or ongoing. Vendor may exercise such suspension right without prior notice to Customer, without any obligation to provide a cure period, and without any requirement to specify the nature, basis, or supporting evidence of the alleged violation prior to, concurrent with, or following such suspension.
6.2 No Procedural Safeguards. No procedural safeguards, escalation procedures, notice-and-cure periods, review panels, appeal mechanisms, mediation processes, or other remedial procedures are provided under this AUP with respect to Vendor's exercise of its suspension rights under this Section 6. Customer acknowledges and agrees that Vendor's determination to suspend access shall be final and binding absent manifest error, and that Vendor shall have no liability to Customer arising from or related to any such suspension, including for any damages, lost profits, business interruption, or other losses resulting from the suspension.
6.3 Reservation of Other Rights and Remedies. Suspension under this Section 6 shall not limit, waive, or impair any of Vendor's other rights or remedies under the Agreement or at law or in equity, including, without limitation, Vendor's right to terminate the Agreement for cause pursuant to the termination provisions of the Agreement, Vendor's right to seek injunctive relief, and Vendor's right to recover damages.
6.4 Continued Fee Obligations During Suspension. Customer shall remain liable for all fees, charges, and other amounts accruing under the Agreement during any period of suspension, including any minimum commitment fees, platform access fees, and overage charges, regardless of whether Customer is able to access or use the Platform during such period. Suspension shall not toll, defer, or otherwise affect Customer's payment obligations under the Agreement.
6.5 Restoration of Access. Following any suspension under this Section 6, Vendor may, in its sole discretion, restore Customer's access to the Platform upon such terms and conditions as Vendor deems appropriate, which may include the implementation of additional security measures, usage restrictions, or monitoring requirements. Vendor shall have no obligation to restore access on any particular timeline or at all.
7. MODIFICATION OF THIS AUP
7.1 Right to Modify. Vendor reserves the right to modify, amend, supplement, or replace this AUP at any time during the Term, in Vendor's sole discretion, by posting an updated version to Vendor's customer portal, delivering an updated version through the Platform's administrative console, or providing written notice to Customer at the notice address or email address specified in the Agreement. The effective date of any modification shall be the date specified in the updated AUP or, if no date is specified, the date on which the updated AUP is posted or delivered.
7.2 Acceptance Through Continued Use. Continued use of the Platform by Customer or any Authorized User following the effective date of any modification to this AUP shall constitute Customer's unconditional acceptance of the modified AUP. Customer is responsible for periodically reviewing the current version of this AUP as posted on Vendor's customer portal.
7.3 No Separate Consent Required. No separate consent, acknowledgment, signature, electronic acceptance, or other affirmative act from Customer is required for modifications to this AUP to take effect. Customer's sole remedy in the event that it objects to any modification to this AUP shall be to cease use of the Platform and, if applicable, to exercise any termination rights available to Customer under the Agreement, subject to the terms and conditions thereof.
8. RELATIONSHIP TO THE AGREEMENT
8.1 Incorporation into the Agreement. This AUP is incorporated into and forms an integral part of the Agreement. The rights and obligations set forth in this AUP are in addition to, and do not limit, any other rights, obligations, restrictions, or requirements set forth in the Agreement or any other Exhibit thereto.
8.2 Conflict Resolution. In the event of a conflict or inconsistency between this AUP and the body of the Agreement (including its other Exhibits), the terms of the Agreement shall control unless this AUP expressly states that a particular provision of this AUP is intended to supersede or prevail over a specific provision of the Agreement.
8.3 Defined Terms. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this AUP shall have the meanings given to them in the Agreement. Where this AUP uses a defined term in a manner that is narrower or more specific than the definition provided in the Agreement, the narrower or more specific usage shall apply for purposes of this AUP only.
8.4 Scope of Exhibit D. This Exhibit D consists solely of this Acceptable Use Policy. For the avoidance of doubt, no subcontractor list, subprocessor registry, data processing addendum, security schedule, service level agreement, or other schedule, annex, or appendix is appended to, incorporated within, or otherwise forms part of this Exhibit D.
